title: Continuous differentials of a formal power-series quotient
statement: Let $F$ be a field, $n\ge0$, $D=F[[t_1,\ldots,t_n]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], $\mathfrak n=(t_1,\ldots,t_n)\subset D$, and $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_s)$ with each $f_j\in\mathfrak n$. Let $R=D/I$ and $\mathfrak n_R=\mathfrak nR$. Define the module of continuous $F$-differentials of $R$ as $\widehat\Omega_{R/F}=\varprojlim_r\Omega_{(R/\mathfrak n_R^r)/F}$ (Kähler differentials [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], transition maps induced by the quotient maps), with the $F$-derivation $\widehat{\mathrm d}:R\to\widehat\Omega_{R/F}$, $x\mapsto(\mathrm d(x\bmod\mathfrak n_R^r))_r$. Then the $R$-linear map from the cokernel of $R^{\oplus s}\to R^{\oplus n}$, whose $j$-th column is $(\partial f_j/\partial t_i\bmod I)_i$, where $\partial/\partial t_i$ is the termwise formal partial derivative [def-trf-formal-power-series-partial-derivative], to $\widehat\Omega_{R/F}$ sending the class of the $i$-th basis vector $e_i$ to $\widehat{\mathrm d}(t_i\bmod I)$ is well defined and is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0C4D, algebraically closed proof paragraph: the power-series Jacobian presentation of continuous differentials; Algebra Tags 00RS, 00RU and 00RX for the quotient and polynomial analogues.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-formal-power-series-continuous-free] to $D=F[[t_1,\ldots,t_n]]$. It identifies the continuous differential module $\widehat\Omega_{D/F}$ with the free $D$-module on the coordinate differentials $\widehat{\mathrm d}(t_i)$ and gives the termwise derivative formula for every $h\in D$.

source.place: Algebra Tag 00RX (lemma-differentials-polynomial-ring) and Tag 02HQ (lemma-differential-mod-power-ideal), via the continuous free-module statement cited in this step.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-formal-power-series-continuous-conormal] to $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_s)$. Its exact sequence identifies $\widehat\Omega_{R/F}$ as the cokernel of the map $R^{\oplus s}\to\widehat\Omega_{D/F}\otimes_D R$ sending the $j$-th basis vector to the image of $\widehat{\mathrm d}(f_j)$.

source.place: Algebra Tag 00RU (lemma-differential-seq) and Tag 02HQ (lemma-differential-mod-power-ideal), via the continuous conormal statement cited in this step; 00RS is the transitivity sequence, not the quotient conormal sequence.

proof.text: By the formula in [lem-trf-formal-power-series-continuous-free], for each relation $f_j$ one has $\widehat{\mathrm d}(f_j)=\sum_i(\partial f_j/\partial t_i)\widehat{\mathrm d}(t_i)$. After tensoring with $R$, the first map in the preceding exact sequence is therefore represented in the free basis $\widehat{\mathrm d}(t_i)$ by the matrix whose $j$-th column is $(\partial f_j/\partial t_i\bmod I)_i$; the derivative is the formal one of [def-trf-formal-power-series-partial-derivative].

source.place: Matrix identification from the cited continuous free-module formula and the formal derivative definition; compare the polynomial Jacobian presentation in Curves Tag 0C4D (lemma-nodal), first proof paragraph.

proof.text: The cokernel of that matrix map is, by Step 2 and the basis isomorphism of Step 1, canonically isomorphic to $\widehat\Omega_{R/F}$. The induced map sends the class of the $i$-th standard basis vector to $\widehat{\mathrm d}(t_i\bmod I)$, exactly as in the statement, so it is well defined and an isomorphism.
